rationale: A special edition on the launch of ImpactBench: the launch and its results on page one, the label, the method, its validation, its supporters and its origins on page two.

assignments.angle: MIT Media Lab and partners release an open benchmark, and a consumer label built from it, after 48,540 simulated conversations.

photo.subject: The exterior of the MIT Media Lab building
photo.why: The project is led from the MIT Media Lab.

assignments.angle: ImpactBench starts from a gap in how AI is tested, and in who builds the tests.
ImpactBench's first release finds a gap of more than 15 points, widest for psychological outcomes, with learning and agency weakest.
ImpactBench tests whole conversations, and reports where failures build turn by turn and where teen scenarios differ.
The AI Nutrition Label condenses more than 800 metrics into a profile a parent or a teacher can read at a glance.

photo.subject: A nutrition facts label on a food package
photo.search: Nutrition Facts label saturated fat per serving
photo.why: The AI Nutrition Label is modeled on food nutrition labels.

assignments.angle: Clinicians and educators propose behaviors to measure, and a six-step pipeline turns each into simulated conversations.
ImpactBench publishes its own validation figures, including where agreement among experts was low.
Statements on the ImpactBench site point to the EU AI Act and to the lack of shared success metrics.
Eighty experts from more than 40 institutions met at MIT; a team of 20 is named on the benchmark.

rail.point: ImpactBench says models are evaluated by researchers and not by the companies that build them.
The platform offers views for the public, for industry and for researchers.
Simulated users’ messages include typos and autocorrect artifacts to mirror authentic use.
Creativity passed 80.5 percent of positive metrics, one of the common strengths.
ImpactBench does not name a single best model and imposes no single weighting.
Scores describe behavior under controlled stress tests, not how often it occurs in ordinary use.
Models offered diagnoses and recommended medication without clinician oversight.
The headline view scores each area from red, consistently undermines, to green, consistently supports.
The Media Lab’s Cyborg Psychology group lists emotional dependence on AI companions among its research subjects.
Domain experts can share their expertise to be invited to review a metric in an area they know best.
